benign-01-internal-notice.eml.label: benign
benign-01-internal-notice.eml.note: internal, fully aligned authentication, no links

benign-02-known-supplier-invoice.eml.label: benign
benign-02-known-supplier-invoice.eml.note: allowlisted supplier, aligned auth, PDF matches its bytes

benign-04-industry-newsletter.eml.label: benign
benign-04-industry-newsletter.eml.note: bulk sender: Return-Path and Reply-To both differ from From, which is normal for mailing platforms and must not alone raise the action

hard-01-forwarded-spf-break.eml.label: benign
hard-01-forwarded-spf-break.eml.note: SPF fails because a mailing list rewrote the envelope, but DKIM still aligns. The single most important false positive to get right.

hard-02-genuine-mfa-reset.eml.label: benign
hard-02-genuine-mfa-reset.eml.note: textbook phishing language used entirely legitimately by the real IdP. Tests whether ES-SOC-005 alone can push a message to quarantine.

hard-03-first-contact-invoice.eml.label: benign
hard-03-first-contact-invoice.eml.note: first contact plus payment language plus an attachment, all legitimate. Tests that context signals do not accumulate into a quarantine.

hard-04-marketing-shortener.eml.label: benign
hard-04-marketing-shortener.eml.note: shortener, urgency, and anchor text that does not match the href, all from a genuine marketing platform. The hardest benign case in the set.

hard-05-compromised-supplier.eml.label: malicious
hard-05-compromised-supplier.eml.note: fully authenticated, allowlisted, established sender, and still malicious because the account is compromised. Authentication cannot detect this; only the payment-change request can. Correct outcome is investigate rather than quarantine: on the evidence available to the tool this is indistinguishable from a genuine bank-detail change, and the control that catches it is a human telephoning a number held on file, not an automated block.

hard-06-internal-script-attachment.eml.label: benign
hard-06-internal-script-attachment.eml.note: a directly executable attachment sent legitimately by a known internal colleague. Tests that extension category alone does not quarantine.

phish-01-credential-harvest.eml.label: malicious
phish-01-credential-harvest.eml.note: SPF fail, DMARC fail, subdomain spoof of the protected domain, credential request with a deadline

phish-02-homoglyph-domain.eml.label: malicious
phish-02-homoglyph-domain.eml.note: authentication passes for the attacker's own homoglyph domain: the case that proves a DMARC pass is not evidence of legitimacy

phish-03-bidi-attachment.eml.label: malicious
phish-03-bidi-attachment.eml.note: bidirectional override in the filename, which has no innocent explanation

phish-04-macro-disguised-docx.eml.label: malicious
phish-04-macro-disguised-docx.eml.note: payment redirection, macro project inside a .docx, and a forged Authentication-Results header from an untrusted hop
